geometry.rules: A cave is entered at its `mouth.anchor` (the middle column of the mouth) from its `mouth.front` (tools/mines.py frame(): north means the player stands north and the passage runs +z; south runs -z; west runs +x; east runs -x; u runs across, +x on a north or south front and +z on a west or east one; d runs into the hill, d = 0 is the mouth line). The mouth floor y0 is the lower median of the heightmap's ground (tools/ground.py, rounded) over row d = -1, u = -(hw+1) .. hw+1, where hw is the first passage's half width. Rows, in order: d = 0 the mouth (floor y0; timber posts at u = +-(hw+1) from y0+1 to y0+H and a beam of timber over u = -(hw+1) .. hw+1 at y0+H+1, H the first passage's height; one hanging lantern under the beam at u = 0); then the `passages` one after another, the first an `incline` of `length` = drop rows d = 1 .. drop, row d with floor top ft = y0 - d + 1 (a stair block facing the mouth's side, as the mining caves), the later ones level `drift` or `crawl` rows at yh = y0 - drop; then the `antechamber` if any (a room of half width `half_width`, `length` rows, `height`), then, if the cave has a gate, the door row (one row, half width door_half_width, height door_height, filled with barrier blocks over its whole cross-section) and `link_rows` rows of drift at half width door_half_width; then the oval `chamber`: centred on u = 0 at row dc = (its first row) + rz, a cell (u, d) is inside when u*u*rz*rz + (d-dc)^2*rx*rx <= rx*rx*rz*rz, air from yh+1 to yh+h over a floor at yh. Every row of a passage, link or room is air from its floor top + 1 to its floor top + height over u = -hw .. hw (the room's half width); an incline row whose least ground over u = -(hw+1) .. hw+1 is under its air top + 1 + cover_min.passage is an open cutting (air up to the higher of the ground and the air top, plus clear_above), every other row, and every room, must be a tunnel: ground over its air top >= the cover_min of its kind (passage 3, room 4). At most max_cutting_rows rows are cuttings. Shell: every non-air cell in the same column hull that lies within `margin` (passage 2, room 3, cutting 1) in x and z of an air column, from the lowest air cell minus the margin to the highest air cell plus the margin, is the cave's shell block, but only at or under ground - 1 (at or under ground next to a cutting). Wherever an air column's floor is more than one block over the ground, the cells from ground + 1 up to the floor (under a stair, under a floor, under a mouth post) are `fill` of the shell block, at most max_fill deep; the mouth's posts stand on such fill the same way. Lanterns stand on posts (a spruce fence block with a standing lantern on it, never a light block): on every row d of a level passage with (d - the passage's first row) % lantern_every == lantern_every // 2, alternately on the left and right wall column (u = -hw first, then +hw, counting across the whole cave), on the antechamber's two end corners (u = +-(half_width - 1) at its last row minus one), and four in the chamber at u = +-round(0.6 rx), d = dc +- round(0.55 rz). A chamber feature `columns` puts two full-height columns (the cave's column block) at u = +-round(0.5 rx), d = dc; `crystal` stands amethyst clusters (facing up) on the floor at the chamber cells the hash h32(seed, sid(cave id), u, d) orders first (tools/mines.py's mix; ties by (u, d)), `crystal_count` of them, skipping lantern posts and any cell with (u/rx)^2 + ((d-dc)/rz)^2 under 0.16. Rounding is Python's round(). The Habitat Block of a part replaces the floor cell at that part's centre (the chamber's centre; the antechamber's middle).
